cards.text: Paul, an apostle (Gal 1:1), is writing to the churches of Galatia (Gal 1:2), and he's just told them how the leaders in Jerusalem, Cephas among them, gave him the right hand of fellowship (Gal 2:1, 9). Cephas is Peter, one of Jesus' twelve apostles (Matt 10:2; John 1:42). So you'd think it's all handshakes from here, but then Cephas comes to Antioch, and friend, it gets AWKWARD.

cards.question: When Cephas comes to Antioch, what does Paul do?

cards.text: Not a long sigh, not a vague post online, TO HIS FACE. Paul says Cephas stood condemned, so let's back up and see why.
Here's the backstory. Before certain men came from James, another of those leaders in Jerusalem (Gal 2:9), Cephas had a regular habit at mealtime.

cards.question: Before the men from James came, Cephas used to eat with the ___.

cards.text: Then the men from James arrive, and Cephas starts to draw back and separate himself. It's like the coworker laughing at all your jokes until the boss walks in, and suddenly he is VERY interested in his phone.

cards.question: Why does Cephas pull away from the Gentiles once the men from James arrive?

answers.text: He was afraid of the circumcision group
He was angry with the Gentiles
He was called back to Jerusalem

cards.text: And Cephas isn't the only one: the other Jews join him too. It's like one person leaves the group chat, and then your phone just goes: left, left, LEFT.

cards.question: Paul calls what Cephas and the other Jews are doing ___.
Barnabas, Paul's own partner in ministry (Acts 13:2), stays out of it.

cards.text: EVEN BARNABAS, friend. When Paul sees they're not walking in line with the truth of the gospel, he speaks up to Cephas.

cards.question: Paul pulls Cephas aside and talks to him privately.

cards.text: In front of them all, Paul asks him, “If you, who are a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?” Friend, that is NOT the kind of question you want to hear with everybody watching.

cards.question: What is Paul pointing out with his question to Cephas?

answers.text: He lives like a Gentile but pushes Gentiles to live like Jews
He never once sat down to eat with any Gentiles
He should never have come to Antioch at all

cards.text: Then Paul gets to the heart of it, and friend, this is the MAIN EVENT. He says even Jews by birth like himself know something about how a person is justified.

cards.question: According to Paul, how is a person justified?

cards.text: So Paul says Jews like him have believed in Christ Jesus too, so they may be justified by faith in Christ. Friend, if trying harder could do it, I'd have stamped my way out of that junk drawer all by myself.

cards.question: Paul says that by works of the law, a few people will still be justified.

cards.text: Then Paul raises a hard one, the kind of question that makes the WHOLE ROOM go quiet. If, while they seek to be justified in Christ, people are found to be sinners, does that make Christ a minister of sin?

cards.question: If people seeking to be justified in Christ are found to be sinners, does that make Christ a minister of sin? What's Paul's answer?

cards.text: Then Paul pictures tearing something down and building it right back up. Like finally deleting the app that eats your whole evening, then downloading it again before bed.

cards.question: Paul says rebuilding what he already tore down would prove him to be a ___.

cards.text: Then Paul says something that sounds upside down: through the law, he DIED to the law. Friend, the first time I read that, I just stood on my gold base blinking.

cards.question: Paul says dying to the law means he no longer lives for God.

cards.text: Then Paul gets personal, and friend, this is a BIG one. He says he has been crucified with Christ, and he no longer lives.

cards.question: Paul says he no longer lives, but ___ lives in him.

cards.text: Slow down here, friend. Paul says the life he lives in the body, he lives by faith in the Son of God.

cards.question: What does Paul say the Son of God did for him?

answers.text: Loved him and gave Himself up for him
Rewarded him for keeping the law well
Sent him to teach the law to the Gentiles

cards.text: Paul wraps it up: he does not set aside the grace of God. Me neither, friend, that grace is the only reason I'm not still in the back of a drawer.

cards.question: Paul says if righteousness came through the law, Christ's death would still have a purpose.

findings.problem: The question refers to what Cephas and the other Jews are doing without identifying that action. The choice card does not explain that they have drawn back and separated themselves from the Gentiles, so it depends on the baker remembering earlier cards.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "Stays out of it" uses "it" to point back to the withdrawal and hypocrisy described on earlier cards. The question never says what Barnabas is supposedly staying out of.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This card quotes Paul's entire question, including both living like a Gentile and compelling the Gentiles to live like Jews. Card 14's correct answer merely restates those two clauses, so this card gives away the answer to the following choice.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Christ and Moses are people, while "the law" is not. The three options are not the same kind of thing, and the mismatched option is also easy to eliminate.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
